The tertiary alcohol at 20/1, 9ed7c1fb1c2cc499bbf9, was substantially overpredicted, so the new m203 points sample weaker ratios before applying a generic donor correction. The nitrobenzophenone outcomes 4862e2fb71344ce16021, ce14dd2481560a984aea, and 08812206a257481691c4 showed compact or much less delayed elution than predicted, motivating a dedicated m177 curve. In contrast, diphenyl sulfoxide aa83ae83c0fa0cc37777 was strongly underpredicted at 10/1, so its response must be separated from the nitrocarbonyl behavior. The acid outcome 129036e0bccc4ff7e848 confirmed that strong surface character can produce very early elution, while d43d692e19100ebe5646 remained a distinct intermediate acid response. Oxygen-rich d1172a49fca1e196a59f showed a large V2 underprediction, and donor-rich 48853fd78c77153b963a showed a similar completion failure; the new m107, m125, m118, m205, and m206 curves target those gaps. The m127 outcomes a3ae677aae8a8faf5786 and c82167c626a1495ef750 had opposing onset behavior under different loading, keeping the loading interaction unresolved. The batch therefore emphasizes discriminating local curves rather than transferring one global polarity or nitrogen adjustment.","batch_rationale":"The batch repairs several high-impact failure regions and gives the retrained model structured contrasts. Four nitrobenzophenone points, three tertiary-alcohol points, and three sulfoxide points distinguish compact, donor-driven, and delayed strong-surface responses. Oxygen-rich curves for m107, m125, and m118 target the repeated late-V2 underprediction region. Acid and charged P/O points test chemically distinct early or nonlinear regimes. Donor-containing m205 and m206 points provide ratio and loading contrasts tied to recent measured failures. Fused aza, nicotinate, and oxime rows extend basic and N/O family coverage. The m127 neutral aromatic ketone points add a loading-sensitive control for correction leakage. Together these experiments cover multiple endpoint behaviors, ratios, loading levels, and chemical families, which should improve generalization across the Row-distribution rather than only correcting one predicted-volume region."}
